question: Wave theory of light explains interference but fails to explain the photoelectric effect completely. Explain why the existence of atomic line spectra also supports the need for quantised energy.

options.A: Both the photoelectric effect and atomic line spectra support the idea that energy exchange between radiation and matter is quantised.
options.B: Atomic line spectra prove that light exchanges energy via continuous, classical wave propagation mechanics.
options.C: Spectral gaps suggest that atoms assume arbitrary continuous levels governed strictly by electromagnetic wave theories.
options.D: Photoelectric variables imply continuous thresholds, while line emission charts align perfectly with classical mechanics rules.
